title: Distributed Workflow Orchestration with Event-Sourced State Machines
subtitle: Temporal/Borg Architecture, Activity Heartbeats and Deterministic Event Replay
problem_statement: A customer onboarding workflow spans 7 asynchronous steps including external KYC verification, credit card billing, and SIM card activation, taking up to 3 days to complete. The current implementation uses ad-hoc cron jobs and database status flags, leading to duplicate billing when workers restart and lost workflows during server deployments.

faded_bug.description: Calling non-deterministic functions (UUID.randomUUID, System.currentTimeMillis) inside event-sourced workflow logic causes replay mismatches.

invariants.description: Workflow execution history must be strictly replayable with zero non-deterministic divergence.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain how Temporal's event-sourcing model reconstructs the state of a suspended workflow without holding thread memory.
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If a long-running activity worker pod is killed mid-execution, how does the heartbeat mechanism prevent duplicate execution of non-idempotent operations?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A developer deploys a new version of the workflow code that reorders two activity calls. What happens to in-flight workflows started on the old code?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: History events for a complex workflow exceed 50,000 events. How does Temporal continue-as-new prevent execution history bloating?

counter_probes.counter_question: Polling database status tables with cron jobs leads to thundering herds, race conditions between workers, and zombie jobs when workers die. How does an event-driven task queue solve this?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Event-driven matching engines with long-polling worker pools and deterministic history logs guarantee exactly-once task handoff and automatic failure recovery without database polling.
